questions.question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate word/words. Choose the correct alternative.

______ behalf of her son, she took the award.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is “**On**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer is option 1 "**On**."
 
• The correct sentence is: *"On behalf of her son, she took the award." *
 
• This means that the woman took the award in place of her son.
 
• **Examples**: 
 
 
• *"On Sunday, we always go to the farmer's market to buy fresh produce."*
 
• *"On the way to work, I stopped for a cup of coffee."*
 
 
 
• The other options, "with," "in," and "at," are not suitable prepositions for this sentence.

**Hence, the correct answer is ***“On"*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Let's see the other given options:**

 
• Option (2) "**With**" is used to indicate accompanying or possessing something. 

 
 
• **For example:** *"She went to the party **with** her friends."*
 
 
 
• Option (3) "**In**" is used to indicate a location or a time period. 
 
 
• **For example: **"*He was born **in** the 1990s."*
 
 
 
• Option (4) "**At**" is used to indicate a specific location or time. 
 
 
• **For example:** *"We will meet at the park **at** 4 PM."*

questions.question:
You are _________ your thoughts very nicely.

**Fill in the blank with suitable participle.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**sharing.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A participle is a type of word derived from a verb that is used for a variety of purposes, such as an adjective or to construct verb tenses. 
 
• Participles have two different types, **the present participle (talking)** and past participle (talked), and participles used as adjectives can form a longer participle phrase.
 
 
• Example: Radha was *reading* a book. (Present participle is used to form a continuous verb tense.)
 
• Max was *annoyed* by the rude manager. (verb "annoy" is used as a past participle)
 
 
 
• The present participle is used for the continuous tenses, and the past participle is used for the perfect tense.
 
• A word that is formed from a verb and **that ends in -ing (present participle)** or -ed, -en, etc. (past participle).
 
• In the given sentence, since the verb "are" is used, the sentence will be in present tense. 
 
• Therefore, we will use the present participle.
 
• From the above explanation, it can be concluded that the correct word to use is "sharing."
 
• The correct sentence will be: You are **sharing**__ your thoughts very nicely.

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

questions.question:
**Direction: Fill in the blanks with the appropriate tense in the given sentence:**

The accomplished artist ______ since he ______ a teenager and today his collection of drawings ______ simply amazing.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'has been drawing, was, is.****'****

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Let us begin with the **third blank.**
 
• For the third blank, we need a singular helping verb "is" **as it is talking about a collective noun** "collection of drawings."**
 
• Therefore, **options 1 and 4** can be ruled out.
 
• Now, the sentence is trying to indicate an action that started in the recent past and is still continuing in the present.
 
• So, we must use** "Present Perfect Continuous Tense"** with the subject **"accomplished artist."**
 
• **Structure: Subject + has/have + been + V1+ing**
 
• So, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

*​​*Correct sentence__: *The accomplished artist __**has been drawing**__ since he __**was**__ a teenager and today his collection of drawings __**is**__ simply amazing. *

questions.question:
Fill in the blanks with the appropriate clause from the options given below.

If I had had a cycle_____________

options.text: I would participate in this competition.
I would have participated in this competition
I will participate in this competition.
I can participate in this competition.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "I would have participated in this competition"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer is 2) "**I would have participated in this competition."**
 
• This is because the sentence is in the past conditional tense, which is used to express a hypothetical situation in the past and its probable outcome. The phrase "If I had had a cycle" indicates that the speaker did not have a cycle in the past and the phrase "I would have participated in this competition" indicates that the speaker did not participate in the competition due to the lack of cycle.
 
• **Option 1)** "I would participate in this competition" is incorrect because it is not in the past conditional tense.
 
• **Option 3) **"I will participate in this competition" is incorrect because it is in the future tense, and the sentence is in past conditional.
 
• **Option 4) **"I can participate in this competition" is incorrect because it does not express the hypothetical situation or its probable outcome.

***Correct Sentence: ***__If I had had a cycle, I would have participated in this competition.
